overall: The AG found the Historical Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by posting insufficiently specific notice topics for its February 8 and March 7, 2024 meetings (Marshall Park, the cave, Goodrich Cemetery, CPA) and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Feb 8 notice topic 'Marshall Park underground rooms' (a man-made cave) was alleged insufficiently specific because it did not say a historic-significance and demolition-delay discussion would occur.
allegations.key_passage: The notice topics before us here informed the public only that a specific park, cemetery, and statute would be discussed; they did not inform the public of the specific issues to be discussed.

allegations.summary: March 7 notice topics 'Marshall Park' and 'Goodrich Cemetery' were alleged insufficiently specific because they did not say what would be discussed about either.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice topics with respect to Marshall Park, the Marshall Park cave, the Goodrich Cemetery, and the Community Preservation Act, were insufficiently specific, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: March 7 notice topic 'CPA' was alleged insufficiently specific, and the acronym was alleged to be unclear to the public.
allegations.key_passage: it is not an acronym widely understood by members of the public and should not be used

allegations.summary: Complaint that the 'underground rooms' wording did not match the 'cave' name used at the meeting; the AG did not decide whether that wording independently made the notice insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: we do not also address whether reference to “underground rooms” and “CPA” further rendered the notices insufficient

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar conduct may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
